Hello, I would really appreciate your help with testing invariance for a second-order CFA. I am testing the following nested models:
(1) configural
(2) metric 1st order (constrain loadings on 1st order factors)
(3) metric 2nd order (constrain loadings on 1st and 2nd order factors)
(4) scalar 1st order (constrain loadings on 1st and 2nd order factors and intercepts on 1st order factors)
(5) scalar 2nd order (constrain loadings on 1st and 2nd order factors and intercepts on 1st and 2nd order factors)

I have followed the examples from previous posts, but I keep getting a scalar 1st order model that fits better than the scalar 2nd order model. Why?
My syntax below. Thank you.

SF =~ c(1,1)*SF1 + c(l2.1, l2.2)*SF2 + c(l3.1, l3.2)*SF4 + c(l4.1, l4.2)*SF5 
CN =~ c(1,1)*CN5 + c(l2.1, l2.2)*CN6 + c(l3.1, l3.2)*CN7 + c(l4.1, l4.2)*CN8
DS =~ c(1,1)*DS2 + c(l2.1, l2.2)*DS3 + c(l3.1, l3.2)*DS4 + c(l4.1, l4.2)*DS5
ID =~ c(1,1)*SS + c(lt2.1, lt2.2)*SF + c(lt3.1, lt3.2)*CN + c(lt4.1, lt4.2)*DS 
'
configural <- cfa(model.configural,
                  data = datainv_db,

messages.subject: Re: 2nd order invariance - nested model fits better
parts: I keep getting a scalar 1st order model that fits better than the scalar 2nd order model. Why?
Because you are adding constraints on more parameters.  Comparing any higher-number model to any lower-number model in your list should yield worse fit for the higher-number (more constrained) model.

Hello, sorry because I am a novice and I really appreciate the support on this forum. I am trying to fit nested MGCFA models to test for first-order and second-order invariance. I've just found out  measEq.syntax from semTools and I would like to ask your help to understand if I got it right. Thank you very much for your kind help, that is much appreciated.

# Configural model (baseline by groups)
configural <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = model_3,
                            data = train_df,
                            group = "db",
                            return.fit = TRUE, estimator ="MLM")

# Metric model (first-order loadings)
metric <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = model_3,
                        data = train_df,
                        group = "db",
                        group.equal  = c("loadings"),
                        return.fit = TRUE, estimator ="MLM")

# Metric model 2 (first- and second-order loadings)
metric_2 <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = model_3,
                          data = train_df,
                          group = "db",
                          group.equal  = c("loadings", "regressions"),
                          return.fit = TRUE, estimator ="MLM")

# Scalar model (first-order intercepts)
scalar <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = model_3,
                        data = train_df,
                        group = "db",
                        group.equal  = c("loadings", "regressions", "intercepts"),
                        return.fit = TRUE, estimator ="MLM")

# Scalar model 2 (first- and second-order intercepts)
scalar_2 <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = model_3,
                          data = train_df,
                          group = "db",
                          group.equal  = c("loadings", "regressions", "intercepts", "means"),
                          return.fit = TRUE, estimator ="MLM")

messages.subject: Re: 2nd order invariance - nested model fits better
parts: I am trying to fit nested MGCFA models to test for first-order and second-order invariance

The sequence you specified seems fine, and consistent with https://doi.org/10.1207/s15328007sem1203_7

Alternatively, you could testing all first-order parameters before testing any second-order parameters: http://dx.doi.org/10.1207/s15328007sem1302_7

I don't know of any reason to prefer one sequence over the other.
